text:
adele: Heads-up — after last night's runtime push I see a KV prefix cache hit-rate drop for chat workloads. overall hit-rate went 82% -> 61% on prod-1. p99 token latency up ~14%.

samir: ugh. any obvious key churn? was there a tokenizer bump or system-prompt change in the deploy?

adele: deploy included tokenizer 0.4.3 and a tiny system prompt tweak (clarified assistant tone). Not sure which is dominant. I captured a few example keys that previously deduped but now missed: 

- before: `kv:chat:assistant_context_v1:sha1:8f3a...`
- after:  `kv:chat:assistant_context_v2:sha1:8f3a...`

The payload is the same conversational prefix text, but tokenized length changed (0.4.2 -> 0.4.3 added an extra token for an emoji).

tia: that matches our internal tokenization diff notes — 0.4.3 splits some Unicode clusters differently. Even small differences cause totally different cache keys.

kai: can we canonicalize keying to be tokenizer-agnostic? maybe key on normalized unicode + normalized whitespace + function-call fields?

adele: proposed canonicalization we tested in staging:
```yaml
cache_key_schema: v1
- normalize_unicode: true
- collapse_whitespace: true
- strip_fields: ["trace_id","request_id"]
- include_system_prompt: true
- include_tool_calls: ["tool.name","tool.args"]
- tokenizer_pin: "tokenizer_v0.4.2"  # optional
```
This reduced churn in staging hit-rate from 58% -> 79% for chat prefix workloads.

samir: important callout: if we pin tokenizer in key we get stability but lose ability to serve newer tokenizers without rewarm. maybe include `tokenizer_version` in the key metadata but normalize the prompt text for the actual key generation. That way keys generated under different tokenizers won't collide unexpectedly but we can still detect equivalent normalized texts.

lee: add numbers from yesterday's profiler:
- prefix cache lookups: 1.2M/s
- misses: 470k/s
- average miss cost (tokens generated before streaming first token): 42ms extra
- p99 extra on misses: 110ms

tia: so misses are expensive because of warmup (KV cache fill + kernel selection overhead). those kernel selection heuristics sometimes pick a slower attention kernel when length distribution in warmup differs.

kai: here's a concrete collision we observed: two requests differing only in `function_call` args order produced distinct keys. example: 
```json
reqA: {"system":"...","user":"...","tool_call":{"name":"search","args":["a","b"]}}
reqB: {"system":"...","user":"...","tool_call":{"name":"search","args":["b","a"]}}
```
If order doesn't matter semantically we should canonicalize those arrays before keying.

adele: good catch. I also found some noise from telemetry: we were including ephemeral `session_meta` map in the key. fix: whitelist fields to include rather than blacklisting.

samir: warmup strategies? pre-warming top-N prefix replays per model region every 15m
- on-startup local cache prefetch for typical PLG patterns (signup flows)
- adaptive warmup: when a prefix miss occurs and it’s high frequency, schedule background warmup for similar variants

lee: perf numbers from an AB on staging with canonical key + offline warmup enabled:
- baseline hit-rate: 61%
- canonicalize-only: 76% (p99 latency -8%)
- canonicalize + offline warmup top 5k prefixes: 87% (p99 latency -22%, cost +4% mem)

tia: memory impact is real: storing normalized strings + metadata bumped in-memory index by ~4%. worth it for 22% latency win.

kai: we should also consider a compact hash key (sha256 of normalized text + sorted tool fields + system_prompt_version). store metadata mapping -> full normalized key for debugging. hashes avoid storing huge keys in the LRU index.

adele: implemented a prototype: `key = sha1(normalized_text || '|' || sorted_tool_signature || '|' || sys_prompt_v)` and an auxiliary map {hash -> sample_text} for 1% of entries for tracing. staging looked good.

samir: any regression risk? the kernel/batching heuristics interplay: if warmup shapes sequence length distribution differently, kernel selector might choose a different kernel for real-time misses leading to perf cliffs. we need to run mixed workload sim where warmup happens concurrently.

lee: ran that sim overnight. summary: with canonical keys + background warmup concurrency set to 8, no regression in kernel selection; p50 improves, p99 reduces. but when concurrency=32 we saw occasional kernel thrash and p99 spike.

adele: ops plan:
1) roll canonicalization (no tokenizer_pin) behind flag in prod on 50% nodes
2) enable offline warmup for top-10k prefixes in region us-west-2
3) keep tokenizer_version baked into hash metadata but not required for equality match for now
4) monitor hit-rate, p99 latency, kernel-choice histogram, and mem pressure for 48h

kai: add E2E checks: ensure function_call canonicalization keeps semantically-equal arg sets equivalent. include tests in perf-suite and unit tests for canonicalizer.

tia: created perf-test ticket: https://redwood.test/org/infra/PROJ-412 "canonical-keying + warmup". I'll add simulated tokenizer diffs to the harness.

adele: i'll schedule the rollout for tomorrow 02:00 UTC, @ops-bot can you prepare a rollback job? :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Rollout job prepared — deploy window 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z, rollback snapshot created.

deploy-bot: Note: will tag the deploy with `canary=kvkey-canonicalize-20260318` and stream kernel-selection histograms to /metrics/kernel_choice.

samir: thanks all. if hit-rate doesn't improve we escalate and revert. otherwise proceed to increase warmup to top-50k over two days.

adele: ok closing loop here — I'll post a short summary in #eng-releases after the canary starts.

(attachments: small profiler CSV, sample keys + token diffs, canonicalizer unit test link)
